title: When Should a Wrist Monitor Withhold a Heart Rate Reading?
grain: One non-overlapping eight-second activity window from an anonymized participant
dataset: PPG-DaLiA daily activities and WESAD laboratory sessions
question: When can a wrist monitor's quality gate reduce error without leaving users without readings for too long?
design: Estimate wrist rate from the strongest physiological-frequency spectral peak. Compare movement-only gating to spectral concentration penalized by movement. Tune on complete DaLiA participants, freeze a threshold and test on unseen DaLiA people and the separate WESAD cohort. Check equivalent coverage, per-person and per-activity error, rejected ECG windows, and sustained gaps.
boundary: The ECG reference is algorithm-derived. The external cohort changes the activity setting; both studies use Empatica wrist hardware. Reported accuracy applies only to the activity and ECG eligibility definitions.
redistribution: Derived window summaries only. No source waveforms, questionnaires or direct participant identifiers are included. Users of the data must observe the respective research-use terms.

fields.ecg_bpm: Chest ECG-derived reference; blank when unsuitable
fields.peak_share: Fraction of in-band power around largest peak
fields.motion: Acceleration variability relative to median vector magnitude
